title: A Ember for the Garden
premise: Tamsin Joubert survives by siphoning memories from the wealthy and selling them to collectors, hiding his gift in the smuggler roads of Thornfell. When Queen Vessaline's purge begins, Tamsin learns he carries a stolen memory that was never meant to be taken: the location of the Door of Aldermere, the only exit from a kingdom erased from maps and history alike. Hunted by the crown's memory-eater, Warden Corvane, and shadowed by Sera, a girl whose forgotten past is tangled with his own, Tamsin must piece together the thirteenth moon's ritual before the door seals for another century. In the end, Tamsin reaches the Door but discovers it opens only for someone willing to surrender their own memories; he gives up his identity to open the way, letting Sera and the hunted pass through while he remains, nameless, as the garden beyond blooms.
about_author: Ivo Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed. They write fantasy about what people keep, what they bury, and what they would trade to forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Tamsin lifts a merchant's wedding memory in the market city of Vell, savoring the easy theft—until the memory resists, whispering a word he doesn't know: Aldermere. His POV establishes his gift, his rules, and his loneliness. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity beneath practiced detachment.

chapters.title: Thirteen Bells
chapters.summary: A royal proclamation floods Vell: all gifted must register before the thirteenth turn of the moon. Tamsin watches neighbors dragged away and burns his safehouse. POV shifts briefly to Warden Corvane, who senses an unregistered thief like a scent. Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Fleeing into Thornfell's smuggler passes, Tamsin finds the mountains themselves hold echoes of stolen memories—his own old thefts, lodged in stone. He realizes the strange memory in his head is a map. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as he understands why the crown wants him.

chapters.title: The Girl Without Yesterday
chapters.summary: Tamsin ambushes a pursuer and finds Sera, a fugitive with no memories at all, her mind scraped clean by Corvane. She recognizes his face anyway. Her POV reveals fragments: a garden, a door, his voice. Beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual damage.

chapters.title: What the Collector Paid For
chapters.summary: Tamsin seeks his old fence, Odile, who confesses she sold him the Aldermere memory years ago on behalf of a client in the palace itself. The hunt isn't about catching thieves—it's about recovering one specific memory. Beat: betrayal reframing everything.

chapters.title: Warden Corvane's Hunger
chapters.summary: Corvane interrogates a captured gifted child, tasting memories to track Tamsin's trail. His POV exposes his corruption: each memory he devours replaces one of his own, and he is running out of himself. Beat: villainy revealed as tragedy-in-progress.

chapters.title: The Erased Country
chapters.summary: In a ruined chapel, Tamsin and Sera find records of Aldermere—a nation deleted from every map after its queen refused the crown's first memory tax. Sera's blankness is no accident; she was born there. Beat: grief for a history no one may speak.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: Corvane torches the smuggler routes, forcing Tamsin to lead refugees through passes only he knows. He must spend precious stolen memories to navigate, each use erasing part of someone else's life he carries. Beat: sacrifice becoming habit.

chapters.title: Sera Remembers Rain
chapters.summary: Touching Tamsin's stored memories, Sera experiences sensation for the first time since her scraping—and accidentally absorbs a memory of Tamsin's childhood, seeing the boy he was. Beat: intimacy and terror, as closeness means consumption.

chapters.title: The Palace's Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Odile's palace contact, Lady Merren, reveals the truth: Queen Vessaline has been consuming her subjects' memories for decades to stay young, and Aldermere's Door is the one thing that can undo her. Beat: the personal hunt becomes a war for the realm's soul.

chapters.title: Turned at the Ford
chapters.summary: A refugee Tamsin saved sells his location to Corvane. Ambushed at the river ford, Tamsin loses his cache of stolen memories—years of other people's lives scattered in the water. Beat: rage and loss; Sera saves him, cementing their bond.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: With the final lunar cycle underway, the mountains begin remembering Aldermere aloud—ghost-lanterns, roads that shift toward the lost border. Tamsin's stolen map-memory starts burning itself into his mind whether he wants it or not. Beat: momentum, inevitability.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Name
chapters.summary: Corvane corners them but falters—he has consumed so many lives he can no longer recall his own mother's face. Tamsin offers him a stolen memory of family in exchange for passage. Corvane takes it and lets them go, hollowed. Beat: mercy as a weapon and a wound.

chapters.title: The Border of Nothing
chapters.summary: They reach where Aldermere should be: a wall of forgetting that makes eyes slide away and names dissolve on the tongue. Crossing requires holding one true memory of the country—and only Sera, empty as she is, can carry theirs through. Beat: hope balanced on a knife.

chapters.title: Inside the Garden
chapters.summary: Beyond the wall lies Aldermere: a preserved country of terraced gardens where the last citizens live in suspended twilight, waiting for the Door to open. Its keeper, an ancient woman, tells Tamsin the price of opening it. Beat: awe undercut by dread.

chapters.title: The Price of Doors
chapters.summary: The Door opens only for a memory freely surrendered—one whole life, given willingly. Sera volunteers herself, arguing she has nothing left to lose; Tamsin refuses to let her vanish. Their argument cracks open both their guarded hearts. Beat: love declared through refusal.

chapters.title: Vessaline at the Wall
chapters.summary: Queen Vessaline arrives with her army, having tracked the thirteenth moon's light. She offers Tasmim immortality and his freedom in exchange for the Door's key-memory. Her POV shows a woman so full of stolen years she no longer knows which life is hers. Beat: temptation wearing a crown.

chapters.title: The Battle of Borrowed Faces
chapters.summary: Vessaline's soldiers attack the garden; the Aldermere defenders fight with weaponized memories, flooding attackers with grief and joy until they collapse weeping. Tamsin turns his thief's craft into warfare, stealing the queen's own stolen years mid-battle. Beat: chaos, ingenuity, mounting cost.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Joubert Was
chapters.summary: Facing Vessaline atop the Door, Tamsin realizes the only memory powerful enough to open it is a whole self, freely given. He chooses his own: every theft, every road, every name. As he surrenders it, Sera screams his name—the last time anyone will say it. Beat: climax; identity traded for others' freedom.

chapters.title: The Door Stands Open
chapters.summary: Nameless and hollow, Tamsin holds the Door wide as refugees pour through into the world beyond, Sera among them, her past restored by the Door's grace. Vessaline, stripped of her stolen centuries by the opening, crumbles into an ordinary old woman. Beat: triumph laced with mourning.

chapters.title: A Man Called No One
chapters.summary: On the far side, Sera searches the crowds for the man who saved them and finds him sitting in a garden, content and empty, tending flowers he doesn't remember planting. She sits beside him and begins telling him stories—starting with a thief named Tamsin. Beat: bittersweet tenderness.

chapters.title: An Ember for the Garden
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Sera's POV: seasons pass. She plants a memory-seed in the nameless man's mind—not to restore him, but to give him something new: a single warm ember of a life not yet lived, theirs together. Somewhere, a new moon rises, the first of another thirteen. Beat: quiet hope, renewal without erasure.
